Thanks for the ping. TL;DR: resend a new invite with explicit TZ (Europe/Paris or Europe/Berlin), and include start/end as local times in the description. Avoid sending an invite that relies on "floating" times or unzoned DTSTART in the .ics.

Steps I recommend:
1) Create a new calendar event in Google Calendar using the event timezone = Europe/Paris.
2) In the description include: "Event times shown: 18:00 CEST (Europe/Paris) / 09:00 PDT (US Pacific)" so recipients see both.
3) Export a fresh .ics and attach it if the customer wants to import.
4) Add a short note about DST in the body: "Note: this event is scheduled in Europe/Paris (CEST). If your calendar overlays a different timezone, please switch to the Paris timezone or accept the event — Google should convert times automatically."

I'll generate the .ics and the calendar web link and post back in 10 min.
